Only the support differs between the three kinds: the ground for boulders and loose stones, the ground plus the neighbouring wall stones' boxes for a wall stone.
- Chunk ids: boulders keep chunk_id; chunks off proxies get StoneSystem.sub_id (a 64-bit hash). Chunks carry their closed cells, so a chunk can be cracked again.
- Chunks lighter than 10 kg are plain items (Stone.hard() is false; they are never in hard_stones()). Their meshes stay exact and centred for the bag.
- Wall stones are drawn holding exactly their counted volume. DryStoneMesh ROUGH went from 0.3 to 0.15 so the volume-exact shape stays inside its box. A struck wall stone is drawn as its real solid with lighter fresh breaks.
- A wall stone is loosened by the push it actually takes, with momentum kept: blow × head mass / (head + stone mass). A god pick gives a 56 kg stone about 63 J against roughly 90–140 J of friction, so chunks crack off first and the stone comes out on a later blow. Before, the whole blow went into loosening. BREAK_STONE_BALANCE stays exact.

Perf work:
- Pieces now split repeatedly after a hit until each is under CELL_TRIS (before, a big spall left one huge piece).
- The flake is cut piece by piece with Fracture.part instead of one big csg_many, with a frame allowed between steps.
- The plan only looks at pieces near each step's region (free face ring by ring, the sampled strip). Results are identical: bench checksum unchanged at 950.289379418739.
- The plan is split across frames (_plan_paced).
- A rock is drawn as one mesh (2 draw calls) instead of one mesh per piece. A heavily worked rock had reached 98 pieces, about 196 draw calls.
- Native god-pick bench (CPU clock): the longest frame per hit went from 115 ms to 24 ms (median 13). Total CPU per hit did not change (median ~50–90 ms, max ~300 ms), because it is bound by the CSG operations, now spread over 5–40 frames.

**Browser target not met:** the ≤ ~50 ms per hit goal is not reached on heavily worked sandstone. Granite frames run median 23 / max 78 ms; sandstone median 57 / max 135 ms. These numbers are wall-clock under hub load ~60 and very noisy: the same hit measured 350 ms in one run and 908 ms in the next. One CSG step cannot be split further; I tried smaller pieces (CELL_TRIS 140) and it was 33% slower overall with no frame gain, so I kept 240.

Also changed (shared tests): break_bot._swing_stone accepts the router's built_stone target, and its loose-stone count includes chunks cracked off wall stones. stone_bot and play_bot now check that light chunks go to the bag via E, and hold a hard chunk when there is one.
